title: The ordinary open tensor quotient square on modules
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell with its ring of integers and uniformizer, independent coefficient and scheme universes, and the integral open coefficient operations for an open immersion j:X -> V and a generator-normalized tensor comparison theta [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Write B_(W,k)=(O_E/varpi^(k+1))_W, S_n^W=Res_(B_(W,n+1)->B_(W,n)) [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], and J_k for finite open extension by zero. Fix n and an ordinary isomorphism e:S_n^X J_(n+1) -> J_n S_n^V carrying every extension generator to the generator with the same underlying section. For every completed integral module sheaf M on X, the ordinary coefficient quotient tau_n [def-sf-finite-reduction-computation] on JM followed by S_n^V(theta_n(M)) equals theta_(n+1)(M) followed by J_(n+1)(tau_n(M)) and e on the smaller scalar reduction of M. This is an equation on ordinary module sheaves, before passing to complexes; no K-flatness assumption is used.

proof.text: Apply injectivity of the larger-level coefficient ordinary scalar adjunction Hom equivalence. Apply extensionSection_ext from OpenScalarTransitionCompatibility to the two transposes: it suffices to compare their values on the completed extension generators. This extensionality theorem uses the localized extension adjunction and its direct-sum unit normalization.

Prove the quotient-section calculation first for arbitrary sheaves of rings and scalar adjunctions, using quotientSectionUnitLaw and QuotientMateLaw.app_eq from CoefficientExtensionAssociationQuotientUnits. Specialize this generic helper to the actual integral coefficient projections. Use nativeUnit_eq to obtain quotient_unit_section, as an HEq retaining the restricted section carrier. Apply this on V to the left composite and use restrict_apply_heq from CoefficientExtensionOrdinaryStrictTensor. TensorComparison.generators evaluates both tensor comparisons.

Use finiteSection_map from OpenSystemUnitSections to move the X quotient through finite extension on the right composite. Apply quotient_unit_section on X. Apply HEq congruence to hgen and this section equality, identifying the two remaining finite generators. The endpoints have the same carrier, so eq_of_heq closes the equality of transposes and hence the original square. The formulas are uniform for n=0, zero modules, and empty extension sums.

lean.statement:
theorem integralOpenTensorModuleQuotientSquare
    (tensor : IntegralOpenReduction.TensorComparison l E j o) (n : ℕ)
    (ordinary : normalizedDVRModuleRes l E X (Nat.le_succ n) ⋙
          IntegralOpenReduction.finiteExtension l E j o (n + 1) ≅
        IntegralOpenReduction.finiteExtension l E j o n ⋙
          normalizedDVRModuleRes l E V (Nat.le_succ n))
    (hgen : ∀ (M : normalizedDVRModules l E X n) (W : V.ProEt)
        (a : W ⟶ IntegralOpenReduction.openObject j),
        HEq (fun x : ((normalizedDVRModuleRes l E X (Nat.le_succ n)).obj M).val.obj
            (op ((IntegralOpenReduction.sliceSite j).obj (Over.mk a))) ↦
          (ordinary.hom.app M).val.app (op W)
            (IntegralOpenReduction.finiteExtensionSection l E j o (n + 1)
              ((normalizedDVRModuleRes l E X (Nat.le_succ n)).obj M) W a x))
          (fun x : M.val.obj (op ((IntegralOpenReduction.sliceSite j).obj (Over.mk a))) ↦
            IntegralOpenReduction.finiteExtensionSection l E j o n M W a x))
    (M : scalarReductionSource l E X) :
    (coefficientOrdinaryQuotient l E V (Nat.le_succ n)).app
        ((IntegralOpenReduction.extension l E j o).obj M) ≫
      (normalizedDVRModuleRes l E V (Nat.le_succ n)).map
        ((tensor.ordinary n).hom.app M) =
    (tensor.ordinary (n + 1)).hom.app M ≫
      (IntegralOpenReduction.finiteExtension l E j o (n + 1)).map
        ((coefficientOrdinaryQuotient l E X (Nat.le_succ n)).app M) ≫
      ordinary.hom.app ((scalarReductionExtension l E X n).obj M)
